text:
eve: Quick sync — Beckett (enterprise) asked for a reserved private deployment window next month; they need HSM/KMS, strict egress controls, and a guaranteed burst slot for demo days. Can product/eng/infra/security confirm feasibility?

maya: Thanks — timeline is ~May 10-20 for pilot, GA later. Customer will sign a short-term reserved capacity contract if we can guarantee slots + audit logs.

ashwin: Runtime note: we can carve a priority lane but need to pin a model variant (quantized) and prewarm KV cache. Without that, tail latency during bursts will spike.

laila: Infra: we can reserve 2 nodes in the private cluster and attach HSM, but networking lock-down (no public egress) requires a ticket to netops. Also need disk encryption keys rotated into their KMS.

sam: Security: we require an architecture review and an acceptance checklist: (1) HSM key policy, (2) audit log retention policy, (3) attacker surface review for private control plane. No go until review passes.

maya: Product asks: define launch criteria so Beckett can sign. Minimal: reserved capacity + HSM + canary with <150ms p95 on 2k concurrent tokens. Also want a rollback window and documented fallback to hosted models if private node fails.

ashwin: Proposed canary plan: 24h canary on the reserved nodes, synthetic load at stepped qps, metrics: p95 latency, OOMs, token cost. If p95 > 200ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows -> auto-cutover to fallback.

ashwin: quick config snippet for prewarm / reservation:
```
reserved_pools:
  - name: beckett-priority
    nodes: 2
    model_variant: gptq-8bit-16k
    prewarm_kv: true
    burst_window: 30m
```

laila: I'll open infra tickets: NET-472 (egress lock), KMS-118 (key rotation), NODE-909 (node reservation). ETA for infra changes: 6 business days after ticket approval.

sam: I'll trigger a security pre-review. Need design doc linked. Please include dataflow diagram and list of exported metrics.

eve: I'll draft the customer-facing agreement with the launch criteria and fallback language. Will ping legal for the limited SLA clause.

maya: Can we get an eng + infra commit for a staging run by Apr 28 so we can do the 24h canary in early May?

ashwin: Realistic: dev work + infra tickets — 8 business days. If infra starts today, staging run by Apr 29 is tight but possible. Need a runtime owner for the canary run.

maya: assigning owners: ashwin (runtime owner), laila (infra owner), sam (security owner), maya (product owner).

ashwin: noted. I'll set up the canary job and a dashboard. I'll include these health checks: `p95_latency`, `kv_hit_rate`, `oom_count`, `token_cost_per_min`.

laila: infra will provision nodes after NET-472 + KMS-118 are approved. I'll add a prewarm script in NODE-909.

sam: Security requirement checklist (short):
- design doc (required)
- HSM policy mapping
- least-privilege IAM
- audit log retention (90 days min)
- penetration test quick-scan

maya: Customer wants a short runbook for failover. Can runtime produce a documented fallback route (API-level) and a test that validates it?

ashwin: Yes — we have an api-fallback route: `x-route: fallback-hosted` that swaps model and region. We'll add an automated smoke test that hits fallback and verifies shape + latency.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: NET-472, KMS-118, NODE-909. Links: https://redwood/tickets/NET-472 https://redwood/tickets/KMS-118 https://redwood/tickets/NODE-909

maya: Next steps summary: 1) infra files tickets (laila) 2) security design doc + pre-review (sam) 3) runtime canary + dashboard (ashwin) 4) product draft agreement + runbook (maya/eve) 5) legal loop (eve). Can we check back in 48 hours? :eyes:

ashwin: 48h check-in works. I'll post a canary checklist before then.

laila: I'll update NET-472 with network diagram and estimated maintenance window.

sam: I'll schedule the security pre-review for Tue morning.

maya: thanks all. If blockers pop up, flag here and we'll escalate to eng leadership. :thumbsup:
